title: ASCII Chart Renderer
description: Build an ASCII art chart renderer that creates bar charts, horizontal bar charts, and pie charts from data arrays.

steps.title: Create a vertical bar chart from data
steps.description: Write a `renderBarChart` function that takes an array of numbers and returns a vertical bar chart string using `#` characters. Each bar is one column. Log the chart.
hints: Find the max value to determine chart height
For each row from top to bottom, print '#' if the bar's value >= row height, else ' '
Use ' ' (space) between bars and '\n' for newlines

verification.successMessage: Vertical bar chart renders with # characters!
verification.failureMessage: renderBarChart should create a column chart where the height of each bar corresponds to the data value.

steps.title: Scale bars to fit a maximum width
steps.description: Modify `renderBarChart` to accept a `maxHeight` parameter (default 10). Scale all values proportionally so the largest bar fits within maxHeight. Log the scaled chart.
hints: Multiply each data value by the scale factor and round
Use Math.round() or Math.ceil() for the scaled heights

verification.successMessage: Bars are scaled to fit within the maximum height!
verification.failureMessage: renderBarChart([100, 50, 200, 75, 150], 5) should scale so the max value 200 becomes 5 rows tall.

steps.title: Add labels to bars
steps.description: Modify `renderBarChart` to accept a `labels` array. Display each label beneath its bar. Extend the chart to include a labeled x-axis. Log the result.
hints: After the bars, add a line with labels centered under each bar
Pad labels to match the width of each bar column
Format: bars, then a separator line, then labels

verification.successMessage: Bar chart includes labels beneath each bar!
verification.failureMessage: renderBarChart([3, 5, 2], ['A', 'B', 'C']) should show labels A, B, C beneath their respective bars.

steps.title: Render a horizontal bar chart
steps.description: Write a `renderHorizontalBarChart` function that renders bars horizontally. Each bar is a row with the label first, then a `|` character followed by `#` bars. Log the result.
hints: For each data point, create a row: label + ' |' + '#'.repeat(scaledValue)
Scale data to fit a maxWidth (default 20)

verification.successMessage: Horizontal bar chart renders with labels and bars!
verification.failureMessage: renderHorizontalBarChart should show each label followed by '|' and '#' bars proportional to the data values.

steps.title: Render a pie chart as percentage bars
steps.description: Write a `renderPieChart` function that renders a pie chart where each slice is shown as a horizontal bar with the percentage and label. Log the result.
hints: Calculate total: data.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)
Render each slice as: label + ' [' + '#'.repeat(percent / 5) + '] ' + percent + '%'

verification.test: output.includes('React') && output.includes('Vue') && output.includes('Angular') && output.includes('%') && output.includes('[') && output.includes(']')
verification.successMessage: Pie chart shows each option as a percentage bar with label!
verification.failureMessage: renderPieChart([30, 50, 20], ['React', 'Vue', 'Angular']) should show React 30%, Vue 50%, Angular 20% with proportional bars.
